title: Recipe costing
summary: The cost of each ingredient, of the whole recipe and of each portion.

what: With a standardized recipe you can cost every dish: how much each ingredient, the whole recipe and each portion cost. It's the basis for pricing and for adjusting the content of dishes.
You need four pieces of data per ingredient: the clean quantity the recipe uses, its unit of measure, its trim waste % and its purchase price in that same unit.
formula: Gross quantity = recipe quantity × waste factor
Ingredient cost = gross quantity × purchase price
Recipe cost = sum of the ingredient costs
Cost per portion = recipe cost ÷ yield

variables.name: Recipe quantity
variables.description: Clean, ready-to-cook quantity of each ingredient.

variables.name: Purchase price
variables.description: Price of the product as purchased, in the same unit as the quantity.

variables.name: Yield
variables.description: How many portions the recipe makes.

variables.name: Share
variables.description: What percentage of the total cost each ingredient represents.

steps: Columns 1 and 2: the ingredient and its unit of measure.
Columns 4 and 5: the trim waste % and its factor.
Column 7: the as-purchased price, in the same unit.
Add up the costs and divide by the yield to get the cost per portion.

examples.title: Tournedos with potato galette for 10 portions (illustrative)
paragraphs: Tenderloin: 1.800 kg clean with 30% trim → 2.571 kg gross × $10,000 = $25,714.29.
Recipe cost: $31,064.29. Cost per portion: $3,106.43. The tenderloin is 82.8% of the cost.

notes.text: With each ingredient's share you can adjust the content: negotiate the price of the most expensive ingredients, review proportions (smaller main item, bigger side?) or substitute ingredients within good culinary practice.
Use the same unit for the price and the recipe: if you buy pears by the crate but the recipe uses kilos, convert the price to kilos.
Small savings per dish add up: $2 less on each of 10,000 units sold a month is $20,000 a month and $240,000 a year.

servings.label: Yield (portions)
servings.placeholder: How many portions the recipe yields (e.g. 10)

unit-price.label: Purchase price
unit-price.placeholder: Price of the product as purchased, per unit (e.g. 10000)
unit-price.hint: Use the same unit as the quantity (if the recipe is in kg, the price per kg).

steps.recipe-cost: Recipe cost = sum of every ingredient cost = {recipeCost}
steps.portion-cost: Cost per portion = recipe cost ÷ portions = {recipeCost} ÷ {servings} = {portionCost}
